newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says needs recorded message for EMU stand.
newsitem.headline: Germany says needs recorded message for EMU stand.

text.p: Germany's Finance Ministry joked on Monday it would have to programme its telephone with the message "Three is three" after denying reports it had relaxed its stance on the deficit requirement for European monetary union.

"I mean this ironically, but I could offer to set up a voicemail in the Finance Ministry press office which will always say "three is three' and the criteria will be strictly interpreted," ministry spokeswoman Barbara Eckrich told a news conference.
Eckrich was referring to the requirement that the budget deficits of those nations which wish to join EMU not exceed three percent of gross domestic product.
Her comments came after Finance Minister Theo Waigel denied changing his views on a strict application of the entry test and called reports to the contrary in the British press "unfair".
"Three percent is three percent and it will stay that way," Waigel said in Munich at a meeting of his Christian Social Union (CSU).

The increase in German unemployment to levels not seen since the 1930s has led to speculation that Bonn, with Paris the main architect of the proposed monetary union, would itself fail to meet one of the basic entry criteria.
